passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: The following discussion and analysis of our financial condition and results of operations should be read in conjunction with our consolidated financial statements and related notes appearing elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. This discussion, particularly information with respect to our future results of operations or financial condition, business strategy and plans, and objectives of management for future operations, includes forward-looking statements that involve risks and uncertainties as described under the heading “Special Note About Forward-Looking Statements” in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. You should review the disclosure under the heading “Risk Factors” in this Annual Report on Form 10-K for a discussion of important factors that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those anticipated in these forward-looking statements. In addition to our results determined in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP), free cash flow, a non-GAAP financial measure, is included in the section titled “Key Business Metrics.” This non-GAAP financial measure is not meant to be considered in isolation or as a substitute for, or superior to, comparable GAAP financial measures and should be read only in conjunction with our consolidated financial statements prepared in accordance with GAAP. Our presentation of this non-GAAP financial measure may not be comparable to similar measures used by other companies. We encourage investors to carefully consider our results under GAAP, as well as our supplemental non-GAAP information and the GAAP-to-non-GAAP reconciliation included in the section titled “Key Business Metrics—Free Cash Flow,” to more fully understand our business. Unless the context otherwise requires, all references in this report to “Snowflake,” the “Company,” “we,” “our,” “us,” or similar terms refer to Snowflake Inc. and its consolidated subsidiaries. Unless otherwise noted, all references in this report to our common stock refer to our Class A common stock, which was renamed to “common stock” pursuant to our amended and restated certificate of incorporation filed with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware on July 3, 2025. A discussion regarding our financial condition and results of operations for the fiscal year ended January 31, 2026 compared to the fiscal year ended January 31, 2025 is presented below. A discussion regarding our financial condition and results of operations for the fiscal year ended January 31, 2025 compared to the fiscal year ended January 31, 2024 can be found in “Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations” in Part II, Item 7 of our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended January 31, 2025 filed with the SEC on March 21, 2025. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: Our operations and financial results are subject to various risks and uncertainties, including those described below. You should consider and read carefully all of the risks and uncertainties described below, together with all of the other information contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including the sections titled “Special Note about Forward-Looking Statements” and “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations” and our consolidated financial statements and related notes, before making an investment decision. The risks described below are not the only ones we face. The occurrence of any of the following risks or additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently believe to be immaterial could materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations, or growth prospects. In such case, the trading price of our common stock could decline. You should not interpret our disclosure of any of the following risks to imply that such risks have not already materialized. Risks Related to Our Business and Operations We have experienced rapid revenue growth and have a limited operating history, both of which make it difficult to forecast our future results of operations. Our revenue was $4.7 billion, $3.6 billion, and $2.8 billion for the fiscal years ended January 31, 2026, 2025, and 2024, respectively. As a result of our historical rapid growth, limited operating history, large number of new product features, including those incorporating artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning technology (collectively, AI Technology), and unstable macroeconomic conditions, our ability to accurately forecast our future results of operations, including revenue, gross margin, remaining performance obligations (RPO), and the percentage of RPO we expect to recognize as revenue in future periods, is limited and subject to a number of uncertainties, including our ability to plan for and model future growth and platform consumption. Our historical revenue growth should not be considered indicative of our future performance. Further, our revenue growth could slow or our revenue could decline for a number of reasons, including increased competition; changes to technology, such as changes in software or underlying cloud infrastructure or the increasing prominence of new technology like AI; reputational harm; changes in macroeconomic conditions; and reduced demand for our platform. For example, customers may continue to optimize consumption, rationalize budgets, and prioritize cash flow management, including by reducing storage through shorter data retention policies and shortening committed contract durations. As a result of the foregoing and our rapid revenue growth in prior periods, our revenue growth rate has slowed in recent periods. Any further declines in our revenue growth rate could adversely affect investors’ perceptions of our business, and negatively impact the trading price of our common stock. credit_strengths.text: Snowflake's revenue base expanded rapidly across the three-year trend, with the latest fiscal year materially above the prior period, evidencing durable demand for its data cloud platform. Operating cash flow also rose each year, confirming that the consumption model converts revenue into cash despite reported operating losses. This cash generation underpins the issuer's ability to fund growth without relying on external financing.

The balance sheet carries a net cash position, as unrestricted cash exceeds convertible debt, and free cash flow covers roughly half of that debt. Liquidity is further supported by a current ratio modestly above parity. This provides a cushion against the sector's typical leverage profile, where the median net leverage is positive and the median current ratio is higher.

key_risks.text: The risk-factor passage highlights that rapid historical growth and a limited operating history make forecasting difficult, and that customers may continue to optimize consumption, rationalize budgets, and shorten committed contract durations. These dynamics have already contributed to a slowing revenue growth rate. For a credit reliant on consumption-based revenue, such behavior could pressure future cash generation and complicate debt-service planning.

The debt structure consists entirely of convertible notes, with no aggregate debt line tagged and no short-term borrowings disclosed. This concentration means refinancing or conversion outcomes depend on equity market conditions and the issuer's share price. A partial debt sum from instrument tags may omit other facilities, so the true debt burden could exceed the reported convertible balance.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage is deeply negative because operating income remains in loss, despite a small absolute interest expense. However, operating cash flow and free cash flow are positive and cover a meaningful portion of debt, while net debt is negative after cash. This suggests the issuer can service its convertible notes from cash generation, though the absence of positive EBITDA makes conventional leverage metrics not meaningful.

Free cash flow to debt sits near the sector median, indicating debt-service capacity in line with peers despite the loss-making profile. Capital expenditure is modest relative to operating cash flow, leaving room for debt service. Yet the convertible notes carry no disclosed maturity schedule, so refinancing risk cannot be assessed from the available data, and this gap is material to the credit view.

overall_credit_view.text: Snowflake presents a net cash position with growing operating cash flow and revenue, but persistent operating losses and negative interest coverage reflect a business still investing heavily in growth. The indicative financial risk profile is not meaningful due to negative EBITDA, so liquidity runway and cash-flow durability are the relevant credit considerations. Shareholder returns via buybacks absorb a large share of free cash flow, limiting deleveraging capacity.

Our forward-looking view is that credit quality hinges on sustaining operating cash flow growth while managing consumption optimization and convertible note refinancing. The absence of a debt maturity schedule and reliance on instrument-tag debt data are material gaps. We would monitor revenue growth trends and cash-flow conversion, as a slowdown could erode the net cash cushion and pressure debt-service metrics.

credit_strengths.text: Snowflake 的營收基礎在三年趨勢中快速擴張，最近一個財政年度大幅高於前一期間，證明其數據雲平台的需求持久。營運現金流亦逐年上升，確認儘管呈報營運虧損，消費模式仍能將營收轉化為現金。此現金產生能力支撐發行人無需依賴外部融資即可為增長提供資金。
資產負債表持有淨現金狀況，因未受限現金超過可轉換債務，而自由現金流覆蓋該債務約一半。流動性進一步由略高於一倍的流動比率支持。這為該行業典型的槓桿狀況提供緩衝，其中淨槓桿中位數為正，而流動比率中位數更高。

key_risks.text: 風險因素段落強調，快速的歷史增長及有限的營運歷史使預測困難，且客戶可能繼續優化消費、精簡預算並縮短承諾合約期限。這些動態已導致營收增長率放緩。對於依賴消費型營收的信用而言，此類行為可能對未來現金產生構成壓力，並使債務償付規劃複雜化。
債務結構完全由可轉換票據組成，並無標記總債務項目，亦無披露短期借款。此集中意味著再融資或轉換結果取決於股票市場狀況及發行人股價。來自工具標籤的部分債務總和可能遺漏其他融資，因此真實債務負擔可能超過所報告的可轉換餘額。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率深度為負，因營運收入仍處虧損，儘管絕對利息支出較小。然而，營運現金流及自由現金流為正，並覆蓋債務的相當部分，而扣除現金後淨債務為負。這表明發行人可從現金產生償付其可轉換票據，儘管缺乏正 EBITDA 使傳統槓桿指標不具意義。
自由現金流對債務比率接近行業中位數，表明儘管虧損狀況，債務償付能力與同業一致。資本支出相對於營運現金流適度，為債務償付留有空間。然而，可轉換票據並無披露到期時間表，因此無法從現有數據評估再融資風險，而此缺口對信用觀點至關重要。

overall_credit_view.text: Snowflake 呈現淨現金狀況，營運現金流及營收增長，但持續營運虧損及負利息覆蓋率反映業務仍在大舉投資於增長。指示性財務風險狀況因負 EBITDA 而不具意義，因此流動性跑道及現金流持久性是相關信用考量。透過回購的股東回報吸收自由現金流的很大部分，限制去槓桿能力。
我們的前瞻性觀點是信用質量取決於維持營運現金流增長，同時管理消費優化及可轉換票據再融資。缺乏債務到期時間表及依賴工具標籤債務數據是重大缺口。我們將監測營收增長趨勢及現金流轉化，因放緩可能侵蝕淨現金緩衝並對債務償付指標構成壓力。
